requirements.requirement: Complete product functionality and discoverable real workflows

sources.quote:
Clarification — working apps and real login, not merely a protected preview
The staging milestone requires the actual in-scope Windows and browser applications with their required functionality implemented and connected, including genuine application sign-in and session handling. Deferring deep acceptance is not permission to defer implementation, substitute mock or partial applications, or call a launch-only shell complete. Short staging checks are not proof of full acceptance; known missing or broken required app/login functionality remains delivery work. Ready apps may be staged progressively while the remainder is finished.
The separate public-facing main/marketing website, its finished public content/design and production WordPress migration/cutover need not be completed for this staging milestone if they are not ready. This does not defer the web apps themselves, working account/login routes, required API/backend services, or functionality inside the Sites authoring app. Keep the current public website unchanged unless a separate instruction authorises changing it.
An outer server/edge login gate is additional protection for private staging, not a replacement for genuine CAKE ID/application authentication. An admitted tester must be able to use the application's real login and authorised account-backed workflows; no fake user, shared administrator session, authentication bypass or inert login page counts. Isolated test accounts/data and existing permissions continue. Complete the working app set on both surfaces first, then concentrate on exhaustive acceptance of those exact builds. Label builds STAGED — DEEP ACCEPTANCE PENDING until that later verification is complete.
Jacob's latest explicit decision is to prioritise staging the full in-scope applications on BOTH the web, behind gated login access, and Windows. Deep acceptance follows once all applications are staged. Acceptance is NOT dropped, weakened or marked passed by staging. This sequencing instruction supersedes earlier directions that made complete app/pass/platform acceptance a prerequisite for private staging or candidate downloads. The missed 07:00 milestone remains history; the immediate delivery target is 11:00 Europe/London today, Monday 5 October 2026, for the working app set on Windows and gated web with real app login, not an unsupported claim of final release acceptance.
Scope is the current launch specification, including incorporated Lunar Eclipse requirements, reconciled with 9to1 Post-Release Updates. The Agentic Update from that roadmap is explicitly pulled forward into the current development push under the priority order above; it MUST NOT be deferred merely because older roadmap wording described it as post-launch. Other expressly post-release additions remain post-release unless they are a necessary dependency of the pulled-forward framework/agentic work or a later explicit instruction brings them forward. Existing baseline launch requirements remain launch requirements and MUST NOT be silently deferred. Record exact app/platform applicability rather than blindly reusing the historical 30-app denominator.
Stage real integrated applications and their existing functionality, not replacement shells, mock dashboards or source-only archives. Publish ready apps progressively while completing the rest. Supply usable Windows packages with their required dependencies and a protected web deployment with working navigation. Before private staging, perform a short build/launch/main-workflow smoke check and verify the actual access boundary and isolated test-data configuration. For an editor, include one basic save/reopen check with disposable data. These are staging checks, not the complete acceptance programme. Record remaining defects clearly; do not label an app complete when its principal workflow is still broken.
Web staging must restrict access to Jacob and explicitly authorised testers at a server/edge boundary protecting application routes and private APIs, not just hide the UI behind a client-side login. Use isolated staging accounts/data/storage and no production secrets or customer-data migration. Windows staging uses separate test profiles/data and the existing supported trust mechanisms; do not bypass Home authorisation or disable OS security. Keep paid/live billing, external mail/inference and production cutover disabled unless separately authorised. Block or isolate only an unsafe/unusable affected operation; do not make unrelated deep acceptance suites prerequisites for the entire staging set.
Team A owns Windows/native/runtime work, Team B browser applications, and Team C the single integration/deployment and handoff path. Preserve reviewed work and use the existing private delivery route. Do not start another broad worker rollout or repeatedly reconstruct/retest unchanged evidence. Batch focused checks, return only useful failure summaries, and preserve sufficient execution capacity for packaging, deployment and handoff rather than spending it all on repeated audits.
After the web AND Windows staging set is available, prioritise deep acceptance on those exact versions: full functional/donor parity, accessibility, permissions/privacy, recovery/concurrency, resource and platform matrices, provider integration and release signing/install requirements. Keep every required test and every failure/not-run state. Existing independent validation may continue when it does not delay staging; do not terminate healthy running tests merely to reorder the queue. Production/RC acceptance and acceptedHead remain separate from staged status.
Report web staged n/N, Windows packages available n/N, apps with both applicable staging surfaces n/N, and acceptance verified separately. Provide real URLs/downloads, source/package/deployment identities, known issues and a resumable handoff. Keep artifacts immutable and version later fixes. If execution ends before deep acceptance, preserve the accessible staging builds and pending tests, explicitly unverified; do not claim background work continues or that final release acceptance passed.

steps: Use the packaged app to complete all named core workflows from ordinary navigation; inventory each visible operation and compare the complete canonical product section and retained donor operations.
expected: No inert control, mock state, missing principal function or launch-only shell; every mandatory applicable operation is separately evidenced.

sources.quote: Where an app declares a donor/upstream project, the implementation MUST contain the actual donor source (forked, vendored or otherwise included according to the repository architecture) in the app’s source tree/build graph. The selected donor revision/version and local modifications MUST be traceable.

requirements.requirement: Cross-app canonical artifact integration

sources.quote: * Deep interoperability is mandatory. 9to1 apps are not independent silos. When a target app declares support for an artifact type, links/embeds MUST reference the canonical underlying document/project/entity rather than create an unmanaged duplicate. expected: The same canonical artifact ID and revision is observed; unsupported combinations fail explicitly without flattening or unmanaged copies.

requirements.requirement: All user operations have equivalent typed APIs

sources.quote: Every 9to1 app must expose a first-party automation API whose action surface is exhaustive for user-accessible app functionality. An authorised MCP, plugin, script, agent or other client must be able to perform anything the user can perform in the app through supported UI, subject to the same account, object, platform and security restrictions. APIs must not be intentionally limited to a small automation subset while important user actions remain UI-only.

steps: Enumerate UI operations against the action catalogue; run equivalent disposable operations through UI and an authorised API caller.
expected: Equivalent state, validation, risk, scope, errors, cancellation and audit results; no UI-only mandatory feature or competing implementation.

requirements.requirement: Home permission grant lifecycle and actual dispatch boundary

sources.quote: 9to1 Home is the central permission broker for app APIs. A caller never dispatches a protected action directly to the target app without Home first resolving its permission state. If Home is not open, 9to1 opens it and shows the approval prompt before the target action executes. A caller may submit the request to the broker, but the requested app action remains PendingApproval until Home grants it.

steps: With Home closed, request a protected action; exercise Decline, Block, Accept, 30-day trust expiry, temporary action/time limits, Always Trust warning, scope escalation and revocation before queued dispatch.
expected: Actions remain PendingApproval until authorised; denied/revoked actions have no effect, caller-name spoofing never inherits trust, high-risk and underlying account limits remain enforced.

requirements.requirement: Genuine CAKE ID sign-in and server authority

sources.quote: 9to1 web apps authenticate against CAKEMODS/CAKE ID using a browser-based OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code flow with PKCE or an equivalent secure public-client flow. Desktop, web and open-source/custom clients are treated as untrusted public clients: they receive short-lived user access tokens and never contain provider keys, billing secrets or entitlement-signing secrets.

steps: Use isolated real test accounts to sign in/out, inspect/revoke sessions, restart and request account-backed objects; exercise invalid/expired sessions and client-modified entitlement claims.
expected: Real authorised canonical account/session; short-lived public-client credentials, server-enforced account/entitlement scopes and structured rejection; no fake user/shared admin substitute.

requirements.requirement: Native package dependencies, install, update, repair and rollback

sources.quote: The single trusted installer MUST install Home, all mandatory modules, the selected app and its app-required dependencies. Selecting a second app MUST reuse compatible shared packages. Internal platform package formats may be used; separate user-facing standalone MSIX installers for individual apps are not the distribution model. Native Windows and 9to1-OS use this contract through their supported packaging mechanisms. Browser apps use authenticated shared web services and MUST NOT require a local Home installation.

steps: On each admitted supported native architecture install from the exact installer; select two apps, cancel optional module installation, interrupt update/activation, repair, rollback and uninstall one app.
expected: Home and compatible mandatory/shared dependencies install and are reused; staged/atomic activation or recovery preserves valid install and user artifacts; separate user-facing per-app MSIX is not the required model.

requirements.requirement: Atomic mutations, conflict and partial success integrity

sources.quote: Mutations MUST be atomic at the smallest user-visible operation boundary unless the operation explicitly declares partial-success semantics. When a multi-object operation can partially succeed, the result MUST identify every succeeded, failed, skipped and rolled-back item.

expected: Atomic boundary holds or structured result lists succeeded/failed/skipped/rolled-back items; stale revisions do not silently overwrite accepted work.

requirements.requirement: Durable recovery and consequential-action replay

sources.quote: APIs that enumerate unbounded collections MUST define pagination or streaming. APIs that can produce long-running work MUST expose request/job identity, status and cancellation. APIs that retry or can be replayed MUST define idempotency semantics so an interrupted client does not accidentally duplicate consequential mutations.

steps: Page a realistic data set; start/cancel a long operation; lose the response after an authorised consequential action and resume using the same request/task ID.
expected: No skipped/duplicate records; request/job identity, status/cancellation and idempotent reconciliation prevent duplicated effects.

requirements.requirement: Privacy ceiling, minimisation and cloud/local boundary

sources.quote: Privacy acceptance MUST include automated and manual tests for least-privilege access, unauthorised cross-app data access, cloud/local boundary enforcement, retention/deletion propagation, export correctness, consent/withdrawal, encryption-state truthfulness, metadata minimisation, log redaction, provider failure and jurisdiction-profile changes. A product is not privacy-complete merely because its privacy policy text exists.

expected: No unauthorised content exposure, remote transfer or stale readable cache; encryption-state claims are truthful and logs redact secrets/unnecessary personal data.

requirements.requirement: Errors, unavailable values and lifecycle truthfulness

sources.quote: Unknown, unavailable and empty values MUST remain distinguishable. A value MUST NOT be replaced with zero, false, an empty string or an invented default merely because the provider/backend cannot supply it. Component-specific contracts such as Dulche’s null/Na distinction override this general rule where defined.

steps: Disconnect a required provider, remove a dependency, cancel a pending operation and reopen after supported interruption; compare UI, typed result and audit history.
expected: Unavailable/error/empty remain distinct and structured; clean lifecycle/cancellation leaves truthful recoverable state, no invented success or unexplained data loss.
